title: Local rings of prime and principal localizations
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p\subset R$ a prime ideal and $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. (1) For a prime ideal $Q'\subset A$, let $\mathfrak q=\{r\in R:r/1\in Q'\}$ be its contraction to $R$. Then the natural $R$-algebra map $R_{\mathfrak q}\longrightarrow A_{Q'}$, $r/u\longmapsto(r/1)/(u/1)$, is an isomorphism. (2) For any $t\in A$, put $B=A[1/t]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. For a prime ideal $Q\subset B$, let $Q'=\{a\in A:a/1\in Q\}$ be its contraction to $A$. Then the natural $A$-algebra map $A_{Q'}\longrightarrow B_Q$, $a/u\longmapsto(a/1)/(u/1)$, is an isomorphism.

mathlib_searches.query: The localization of a localization at a prime is the original ring localized at the contracted prime

mathlib_match.how: exact for both clauses, one application each: lines 156-159 give an R-algebra equivalence between Localization.AtPrime (Q.comap (algebraMap R (Localization S))) and Localization.AtPrime Q for any multiplicative set S. For (1), S=R minus p; for (2), the base ring is A and S={1,t,t^2,...}. The equivalence is the canonical fraction map in each clause. Lines read 2026-10-10.
